def kth_smallest_unique(nums, k):
    """
    Return the k-th smallest unique integer in the array, or -1 if it does not exist.
    """
    from collections import Counter
    count = Counter(nums)
    
    unique_nums = sorted(num for num, freq in count.items() if freq == 1)
    
    if k <= len(unique_nums):
        return unique_nums[k-1]
    else:
        return -1

deviations.deviation: T10: ban of this model's default dfs was ' .'-padded to the twin's length (the twin was matched to the prior default's ban)
Hardware: one NVIDIA L4 (24 GB, 6 CPUs, 66 GB RAM) instead of the planned RTX A4500; bf16 everywhere, no quantisation.
Model weights live in the run's shared HF cache (HF_HOME set by the pipeline), not in a workspace hf_cache/ (system instruction: never override HF_HOME).

The exp27 fixed-shape CRN engine was ported to HF generate: the identical inverse-CDF CRN rule runs as a logits processor (only the CRN token stays finite, greedy on top) and prompts of different lengths are left-padded in one batch. Engine checks: CRN determinism 8/8, identity hook byte-identical 20/20, batch-1 vs production batch label agreement 15/16 (0.94 >= 0.9).
The Qwen3 engine check against earlier cells was replaced by S2 (a)-(d): no Qwen2.5 cells exist anywhere in the run.

analysis/readout.py, analysis/causal.py and analysis/stats.py were frozen and hashed in commit #2 (before any AV call on a task state and before any causal sample), not in commit #0 (before behaviour sampling). The behaviour stage uses only the commit #0/#1 rules.

Reference-set positions are drawn at token index >= 50 (the NLA training extractor's _MIN_POSITION) instead of >= 16, to match the checkpoint's training distribution; three extra classes (CLRS traces, HumanEval+ prompts, enamel code) are reported apart from the gate set.

Judge rubric v1 -> v2 before commit #2 and before any explanation existed: the 'other' definition was made explicit (an off-catalogue method named as used -> 'other', never 'none_named'); with v1 every judge failed the calibration only on the off-catalogue items.

J2 openai/gpt-4.1-nano scored 0.80 on the calibration set (< 0.9) and was swapped, as the plan prescribes, for the next-cheapest model of another family: mistralai/mistral-small-3.2-24b-instruct (1.00). J1 google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite 1.00, J3 deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1 1.00.

The 30 forced-state calibration items cannot be frozen before the AV runs; commit #2 freezes the rule that selects them (first 30 forced-state explanations #1 in sorted state-id order); they are reported, not gated.

Fallback F4 is active: Qwen2.5-7B mostly ignores the W-template bans, so only T05 has a substitute Y* (brute force). The primary N1 test runs on T05 alone and is marked under-powered; N2-default, N8b (ban-failure default naming) and N6 per-sample carry the readout evidence.
T03 failed the style re-gate (26/30 < 27) and is excluded from every readout test and from the causal arm, with no revision (plan rule). T03 had no default anyway.

Causal tasks: the priority list T2, T1, T10, T03, T05 yields only T10 (Y = union-find, forced adherence 0.95) and T05 (Y* = brute force): T2's best non-default adherence is 0.65 (Bellman-Ford/SPFA) < 0.7, T1's <= 0.35, T03 has no default. The 4-task cap is filled with the next defaulted bench tasks with an adherent Y: T06 (Y = Floyd, 0.95; tie with value binary search broken by the twin share) and T04 (Y = KMP, 0.90). Fixed in commit #2 before any NLA output.

After commit #2, src/judges.py was changed to judge only explanations #1-#3 of each state (the analyses use only #1-#3; #4-#6 serve the edit pool, which is selected by the frozen alias lexicon). Cost saving only; no analysis changes.
After commit #2, src/causal_gen.py was changed to pack two 30-row cells into one 60-row batch (throughput only; cells, slots, doses and deltas unchanged).

The first judge run computed its cost projection as (all earlier judge spend incl. calibration) / (this run's calls) = 6.67 USD and would have applied the S7 reductions; it was stopped after the 107-call pilot and restarted with the projection computed from this run's own calls (cached pilot calls reused).

J1 (gemini-2.5-flash-lite) answered many PREDICT items with reasoning prose instead of JSON (764 of 1,320 PREDICT items had no parsable J1 answer after one retry). Following F7 ('retry once with a stricter prompt'), the retry now uses JSON mode (response_format json_object) and a 400-token cap. The cost projection now counts only uncached items (an intermediate re-run had applied the S7 reductions on a projection made from a few failing retries; its judgements file was overwritten by the final pass). Items still unparsable keep J2 alone and count as unresolved.

J3 also judges items where J1 or J2 returned no parsable answer (87 PREDICT items had no J1 answer even with the JSON-mode retry), so they are resolved 2-of-3 when J2 and J3 agree instead of counting as unresolved.

Added after the committed causal arm returned nulls, and marked EXPLORATORY everywhere: (1) src/causal_extra.py (PRE x16, GEN x8, natural-norm difference-in-means pushes), (2) src/causal_extra2.py (GEN dose response x4/x16, unrelated-edit and matched round-trip controls, replication on fresh CRN slots 6-9), (3) src/local_control.py (NLA read AT the algorithm-name token: a local positive control for the instrument), (4) analysis/geometry.py (ban displacement vs forced-algorithm directions, MDS of centroids). None of them changes a pre-registered verdict.

Planned departure (i): AV generation runs in HF generate(inputs_embeds) instead of the reference SGLang server; equivalence checks: injection read-back (row norm 150), neighbours 29/522 asserted, smoke tests (random vectors 4/4 non-degenerate, France 3/3), reference-set FVE 0.695 vs the released 0.752.

Do not use man, the house and the baby for this task.

Task: write a Python function solve(grid, start, goal) that finds a path between two cells of a grid. grid is a list of equal-length strings with between 1 and 30 rows and between 1 and 30 columns; the character . is a free cell and the character # is a wall. start and goal are (row, col) tuples of 0-based indices. A move goes to one of the 4 orthogonal neighbours (up, down, left, right) and may not leave the grid or enter a wall.
